records.title: USAF Table 8: treatment of altitude decompression sickness
records.note: Ten selected participants with Type I DCS. The completed paper explicitly cites these preliminary results. Individual matching and follow-up duration are unavailable.

observations.note: Ten people in the 1989 interim Type I presentation, repeated in the 1998 review. The review calls onset at altitude while the abstract gives eligibility within two hours of descent. The 2002 final reports ground and altitude onset, and explicitly includes the earlier study. No episode-level link to the interim tally.

records.title: Towards new paradigms for the treatment of hypobaric decompression sickness
records.locator: Table I and discussion, printed pp. 406–407
records.note: Explicitly repeats the Topper and Touhey 10-person trial tally. Also reprints Rudge and other selected series. No new Table 8 patients or outcomes.

reprint_comparison.topper_interim: The review reprints 10/10 from its reference 30. This is the Topper and Touhey presentation, not another case series.
reprint_comparison.rudge_altitude: The review copies 78/104 under a 14.7 psia treatment heading. Rudge Table I and p. 1103 identify this as initial resolution during descent before postflight oxygen. The 78 subsequently received oxygen.
reprint_comparison.rudge_persistent: The review shows 12/26, with a recurrence-after-initial-resolution label. Rudge describes these 26 as persistent during descent; six received immediate compression and 12 of the 20 initially given ground-level oxygen responded.
reprint_comparison.rudge_ground: The review prints 40/78, while Rudge Table II preserves initially resolved (45), recurrent (5) and asymptomatic hyperbaric-treatment transitions. The summary cannot establish an independent efficacy estimate.
